body: @shawn11ZX are you sure that you really call size() from the same EventLoop as it is assigned too ?
That said I think I can make it safe from any thread....
I am having the same issue occur at random.

Norman, what if the thread of SingleThreadEventExecutor is unexpectedly blocked/long calculates somewhere? So all producers might continue to aggressively fill its queue, which ultimately can cause OOME, but the thread is not available to answer the queue size. So even different thread which called Nio/EpollEventLoop.pendingTasks will have to syncUninterruptibly without being able to report the size of the queue, possibly for long time. When the consumer thread answers the size - it might already be after it consumed most of the queue, so we missed the size at the time we asked for it.
I know size doesn't have to be accurate for such a queue, but I think it is important for analysis purpose that the thread which asks the size will be independent of the thread which consumes the queue. We need to know the size especially if the consumer is blocked somewhere and producers continue to fill its queue. Don't want to wait and depend on the consumer in such case.

Except the OOME, similar behavior to what I described actually happened to us, while we tested new statistic for this queue.

Did you consider using LongAdder for maintaining the size? It maybe could be used inside the queue.

issue.title: (Nio|Epoll)EventLoop.pendingTasks should not block when called outside of event loop

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
### Expected behavior

`EventLoop.pendingTasks` should be (reasonably) cheap to invoke so it can be used within observability.

### Actual behavior

We've been experimenting with overriding `EventExecutorChooserFactory` with more superior load balancing algorithms and found out that it might be quite non-trivial to support pending-tasks load metric (pick the least loaded event loop).

After poking around the code, it seems when querying `pendingTasks` of either `NioEventLoop`  or `EpollEventLoop`, the method [blocks if called outside of said event loop](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/630c82717dd8d822323c9e4a8ad51ea4f8a38f86/transport/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/nio/NioEventLoop.java#L262-L272). Put it this way, it's only cheap to query event loop's pending tasks from within the same event loop. Perhaps I miss some (historical) context for `pendingTask`, but for an uneducated reader, it just defeats the purpose of a method providing visibility into an event loop.

I was hoping to pick up some context on the current behavior of `pendingTasks` and see if we ever want/will to change it.
